transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um... I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has been a little... well, all over the place lately. I hope that's an okay reason to be here? 

It's just, some weeks I barely touch my dinner, which I know I shouldn't do. And then other nights... it's a little embarrassing, but I end up standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else has gone to bed. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in to talk about it, if that makes sense?
Do you think about your weight or body shape when you're deciding whether or not to eat?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I know I'm not in perfect shape or anything, but... it's not really about my weight. When I'm skipping dinner, it's just because I really don't have an appetite, not because I'm trying to diet or anything like that. 

And the late-night snacking... well, I definitely don't feel good about myself when I do that, but I'm not really thinking about my figure when I'm standing in the kitchen. It's just... I don't know, a bad habit, I guess? I hope that makes sense. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I'm not wasting your time.
Do you usually feel guilty after eating, especially after those late-night snacks?

Um... well, yes, a little bit. I do feel bad about the snacks. But... gosh, I hope it's okay to add this, but it's actually not just the eating that makes me feel that way. I just... I seem to get these awful feelings of guilt about almost everything lately. 

Like, I can spend hours just replaying really small things in my head. For instance, I bought this somewhat expensive tube of pigment for painting the other day... or sometimes I might just snap at my husband over something silly... and I'll just sit there feeling like I've completely ruined the whole household because of it. 

It sounds so dramatic and silly when I say it out loud, doesn't it? I know I shouldn't overreact like that, and I try not to. I just want to be a good partner and I worry I'm messing it all up. I hope I'm explaining this the right way for you?
Do you find that you tend to eat more, like during those late-night snacking episodes, when you're feeling stressed or upset?

Oh, um... I don't think so? I mean, I know a lot of people tend to eat when they're stressed, and I definitely don't want to sound like I'm hiding anything from you, but... I haven't really noticed a connection like that for myself. 

When I have those snacks, it's not usually because I'm upset or having a particularly bad day. It just sort of... happens, I guess. I hope that's an okay answer? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate information so I can be helpful.
Do you think the late-night snacking might be related to trying to calm down or feel better in some way?

Um... well, maybe? I guess I haven't really thought of it as trying to calm down, but... honestly, the eating being so all over the place is actually what finally pushed me to come in and see you. 

I just... I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing for my health, you know? But it's been so erratic. Like I said, some weeks I barely touch dinner at all, and then other nights I'm just standing in the kitchen, eating crackers and sweets after my husband has gone to bed. I know it's not a good look, and I really am trying to be better about it. I hope it's okay that I'm sharing all this? I just want to make sure you have the whole picture so you can help me.
Do you think your mood has any influence on when you eat or how much you eat?

Um... well, maybe? I guess I haven't really put it together like that, but... I do go through these stretches where everything just feels so... I don't know, heavy? 

Like, I'll just sit at the kitchen table, and the whole house feels sort of gray and empty, even if absolutely nothing bad has happened that day. I just feel so hollow inside during those times. And I suppose that might be when my eating gets a bit strange, either not wanting anything or just snacking because I'm sitting there. 

I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, because I know I have a good life and I shouldn't complain. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right... does that make sense?
Do you notice that your eating patterns change when you're feeling sad or empty inside?

Um, yes, I suppose so. Like I was just mentioning, when I go through those stretches where the house just feels so gray and heavy... and I'm just sitting there at the kitchen table feeling so empty, even though absolutely nothing terrible has happened that day... I think that probably is when the eating gets the most mixed up. 

I guess I'll either not have an appetite at all, or I'll just nibble on whatever is in front of me because I don't know what else to do with myself. I feel a little silly admitting that, honestly, because I know I shouldn't let my moods dictate my habits like that, and I really don't want you to think I'm not trying to take care of myself. I'm definitely trying to be better. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think you eat to try to improve your mood when you're feeling sad or empty?

Well, I... I suppose maybe I do? I mean, I hate to admit it, but maybe I am looking for a little comfort when I'm just standing there in the dark. 

Like I said before, that's really what made me finally make this appointment. The eating has just been so... all over the place. I really try to be disciplined, but some weeks I just can't even look at dinner, and then, you know, other nights I'm the one in the kitchen with the crackers and sweets after my husband is asleep. 

I know it's not a healthy way to handle things, and I feel awful even saying it out loud. I really am trying to get a handle on it, I promise. I just... I hope it's alright that I'm being so honest about it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can tell me what I should be doing instead.
Do you feel better after eating when you're feeling sad or empty?

Um... well, maybe for a minute or two? I guess it distracts me from feeling so hollow. But then... then I usually just feel guilty. 

Like I was saying, that's really what finally pushed me to come in and see you. My eating has just been so all over the place. Some weeks I barely touch my dinner, and then... well, other nights I'm the one standing in the dark kitchen eating crackers and sweets after my husband has gone to bed. 

I know it sounds terrible, and I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around gorging myself every night. It's not like that all the time, and I'm really trying to be better about it. I just... I hope I'm explaining this okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
Do you think eating helps you cope with your feelings of guilt and anxiety?

Um, maybe a little bit? I do struggle with feeling guilty, even though I know I shouldn't overreact to things. 

I can spend hours just... replaying these really small things in my head. Like, say I buy an expensive tube of pigment, or I accidentally snap at my husband. I'll just sit there and feel like I've completely ruined the whole household because of it. I know that sounds so dramatic, and I really try not to be like that. I want to be a good partner and not make a big deal out of absolutely nothing. 

But when that guilt gets so heavy, I guess eating just gives me something else to focus on for a minute, so I don't have to think about what a burden I'm being. I feel so silly even admitting that I get that worked up over a tube of paint. I really am trying to be more reasonable about things. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking? I just want to be sure I'm giving you helpful answers.
Do you think your eating habits would change if you weren't feeling so guilty and anxious all the time?

I... I really think they would. I mean, if I wasn't always so worried about every little thing I do wrong, I probably wouldn't need to look for that comfort, you know? 

Like I mentioned before—and I'm sorry to keep bringing it up, I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right—that's really what finally pushed me to come in and see you. My eating has just been so... all over the place. I'll go weeks where I'm so good and I barely touch my dinner, just keeping things very light. But then... then there are those other nights where I'm just standing in the dark kitchen eating crackers and sweets after my husband has gone to bed. 

I really do think if I could just get a handle on the guilt and the anxiety, I wouldn't have those bad nights in the kitchen. I want to be healthy and have normal habits, I really do. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need to help me fix this.
Do you think your eating habits are the main problem you're struggling with right now?

Um... yes, I think so? I know I keep bringing it up, and I really am sorry if I sound like a broken record. I just want to make sure I'm being as clear as possible for you. 

But like I mentioned, that really is the main thing that finally pushed me to come in and get help. The fact that my appetite is just so unpredictable right now. Going from being so good and barely touching my dinner for weeks, to those embarrassing nights where I'm eating crackers and sweets in the dark... it just feels like the biggest thing I'm doing wrong. 

The guilt and the worrying are awful, of course, but the eating is the part where I can actually see myself messing up, if that makes sense? I really am trying hard to be better about it, though. I want to get back to normal. Does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm focusing on the right things.
Do you intentionally eat to try to make yourself feel better when you're upset?

Um, well... I guess I do sometimes? I mean, I really don't want to make it sound like I'm just sitting around bingeing every time I get a little sad. I promise I'm not doing that. 

But, um, like I was saying before—and I know I keep coming back to this, I just want to be totally honest with you since it's what finally made me realize I needed to come in—my eating is just so all over the place right now. When I'm having a good stretch, I'm really disciplined. I barely touch my dinner for weeks, and I feel so much better about myself. But then... when I'm really upset or that guilt gets too loud... those are the nights I end up standing in the dark kitchen, just eating crackers and sweets after my husband goes to sleep. 

I know it's not a healthy way to cope, and I'm really embarrassed to admit it. I just... I guess in the moment, the sweets do make the upset feelings a little quieter? I'm trying so hard to stop doing it, though. Is it okay that I explained it that way? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Do you think you eat as a way to directly deal with your feelings of sadness or guilt?

Well, I suppose... yes, maybe a little bit? I really hope I'm not making it sound like I'm just eating my feelings all day, because I'm truly not. I try very hard to keep things under control. 

But it's just... the guilt can get so heavy sometimes. I know I've mentioned it, and I'm sorry to keep harping on the same things, but it's just so hard to explain. I can spend hours—literally hours—just replaying these tiny little things I've done wrong. Like, if I buy an expensive tube of paint pigment, or if I just snap at my husband over something silly... I'll just sit there feeling like I've completely ruined the whole household. Like I'm just this awful burden. 

And when that feeling gets really loud... I guess that's when I end up in the kitchen with the sweets. It's like I just need something to quiet down the thought that I'm ruining everything. I know it's silly to get so worked up over a tube of paint, and I'm really trying to be more rational about it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not overcomplicating it for you.
Do you think eating is your main way of trying to deal with feelings of sadness or guilt?

Um... I don't know if it's the absolute main way, but... well, I guess it is what I turn to when things get really quiet. I really hope I'm not making myself sound completely out of control, because I do try to keep it together during the day. 

It's just... I go through these stretches sometimes where the whole house just feels so... gray and heavy? I don't know if that's the right word for it. But I'll just sit there at the kitchen table feeling completely empty, even though absolutely nothing terrible has happened that day. I know I shouldn't feel that way, and I feel awful even complaining about it because I know I have a good life. But when that heavy, empty feeling sits on me for too long, I think the eating is just... my way of trying to distract myself from it? 

I really am trying to be better about handling it, I promise. I don't want to be doing this. Does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things the way you need me to.
Do you eat as a way to directly try to stop feeling sad or guilty?

Um, I guess... yes, I suppose I do. I mean, I really don't want you to think I'm just stuffing my face every time I feel a little bit down. I'm really not doing that. 

But... well, like I was saying, when that guilt or that heavy feeling just won't go away... I guess the eating is a way to try and make it stop? Or at least quiet it down for a few minutes. I know it sounds terrible, and I'm so embarrassed to admit it because I know I should be stronger than that. I really am trying to find better ways to handle it, I promise. I don't want to be doing this at all. 

Is that... is that what you were asking? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you eat when you're feeling sad or guilty as a way to try and make those feelings go away?

Well, yes, I suppose it is a bit of that. I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record, I just... I want to be honest with you. Actually, my eating being so all over the place is kind of what finally pushed me to come in and get some help. 

I don't want you to think it's just me overeating all the time, because it's not. It fluctuates. Some weeks I'm actually really good—I barely even touch dinner, honestly. But then... there are those other nights where everyone else has gone to bed, and it's just so quiet, and I'll find myself standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets. I know it's not a good habit, and I'm really trying to get a handle on it, I promise. I just... I get so ashamed of myself when I do it. 

I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I'm sorry if I'm rambling, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture without making it sound worse than it actually is.
Do you think eating is something you do specifically to try and cope with your feelings of sadness or guilt?

Um... yes. I think the guilt is a really big part of it. I hope I'm not frustrating you by circling back to this, I really just want to be as helpful as possible. 

But... well, I can spend hours just replaying really small things in my head. Like, um, buying an expensive tube of pigment, or maybe just snapping at my spouse over something silly. And I'll just sit there and feel like I've completely ruined the whole household because of it. I know it sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud, and I'm really sorry if it sounds like I'm making a mountain out of a molehill. I know I shouldn't let those little things get to me that much, and I try so hard to just brush it off. 

But when that awful guilty feeling gets too loud and I can't stop thinking about how I've messed up... I think that's when I turn to the food, just to make it stop for a little bit. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the right way.
Do you feel like you have to eat when you're feeling sad or guilty, even if you're not hungry?

Well, um, I guess I do feel like I have to sometimes, even if my stomach isn't grumbling. I really don't want to sound like I'm completely out of control, because I'm not. But, like I mentioned before, my eating being so all over the place is really what finally pushed me to come in and see you. 

It's just so erratic, you know? Like, some weeks I'm doing really well and I barely even touch dinner, which I know isn't great either, but it's not overeating. But then... there are those other nights where I just feel so awful about something, and everyone else has gone to bed, and I'll find myself standing in the dark kitchen eating crackers and sweets just to feel a little bit better. I'm really trying to stop doing that, I promise. I know it's not the right way to handle things. 

Is that... does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm being clear enough.
Do you think eating helps you directly manage your feelings of sadness or guilt?

Um... I suppose it does help a little bit, in the moment, anyway. I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm repeating myself so much and I really don't want to waste your time. 

But yes, I think it does temporarily quiet things down when I'm feeling that way. It's just... like I was saying, it's that back-and-forth that really scared me into making this appointment. The way it's just so all over the place. I'll be so good for a stretch, just having a tiny bite for dinner, or barely touching it at all, really. And I'll feel like I'm doing okay. But then... well, then I have those nights where I'm just standing there in the kitchen, eating those sweets and crackers when the house is quiet. 

I know I shouldn't, and I really am trying to be better about it. I just... I hope I'm not coming across as completely unhinged. Does that make sense? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
